data.description: Synthesized clicks and drags against a tagged c11 build on the operator's live machine hijack their cursor and focus. On 2026-09-29 a builder's drag-validation scripts collided with Atin working on Hyperion. Give each c11 validation run its own sandbox: a macOS VM or a separate user session, with its own display, so computer-use agents can drive clicks and drags freely without touching the operator's session. Atin's steer: a sandbox or VM per c11 instance is the real fix, probably not Atlas. Deliver a script that stands one up with a tagged build, and update skills/c11-computer-use to prefer it.
data.title: Sandboxed c11 instances for computer-use validation

data.body:
Phase 1 research is pushed. No PR yet, by the brief.

Commit f38c54bae17e3ed6100cbea2e3af597e403cd515 on c11-244-sandbox.
Doc: docs/c11-sandbox-research.md

Recommendation: headless Tart macOS VM, one APFS clone per run, guest-side cliclick/screencapture over SSH. Second-user Screen Sharing is the fallback only if Ghostty cannot create a surface on the guest GPU. In-session virtual displays do not isolate the cursor. Waiting for the orchestrator go before phase 2 scripts and the computer-use skill update.

Scope addition (Atin via Cairn, 2026-10-01): the sandbox must also run the live tests_v2 suites inside the VM (tagged app copied in, suite driven over SSH against the guest socket, results copied back), so live c11 tests never run on the operator's session. Trigger: Atin had to stop another agent's live tests_v2 run because the launched app disturbed his screen.

Phase 2 is on the branch at 7d64986daef07c9c0aed8ba57acaa45761a35551. PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/475

Validated on Atlas:
- Ghostty probe with public v0.66.1: debug-terminals reported runtime=1 and a non-nil ghostty pointer. Screenshot is docs/images/c11-244-guest-terminal.png. No error.OutOfMemory.
- sandbox-up with C11_SANDBOX_HOST=local reported clone_secs=0 and boot_secs=50 for c11-sb-ghostty2. An earlier warm up reported boot_secs=27.
- From the laptop, sandbox-tests-v2.sh ghostty2 tests_v2/test_cli_id_format_defaults.py passed both assertions against the guest socket in about 17 seconds. The clone was then deleted. Golden and the scanner VMs were left stopped.

Open limit: a new serial retriggers Setup Assistant. The FileVault sheet ignored synthesized clicks, and profiles install is gone on macOS 26.6. scripts/sandbox-skip-setup.mobileconfig is in the tree and is not installed. The guest account password is still admin. Password SSH is off.

The c11-computer-use skill source is updated. The installed copy was not synced. After merge, run scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh c11-computer-use.

Repair push 2fc5aace96e738cc16fe51593d9a4b1607cdaf05 on https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/475.

sandbox-up now takes --app-source. local-app (the default) is still a .app path copied from the invoking machine. atlas-build is the reserved source for a later branch build on the Tart host. It exits before SSH. The script does not install Xcode and does not wait for it. Both sources are required to leave one .app in ~/.c11-sandbox/apps/<run-id>/ on the Tart host; the boot path only reads that directory.

Checked locally: --app-source atlas-build, --app-source=atlas-build, and C11_SANDBOX_APP_SOURCE=atlas-build each exit 1 with that message. An unknown source is rejected. A local-app path still fails on a missing bundle before SSH. No guest was booted for this push.

Repair push a6815d091b25e92e2fcf708fef40befa7d6fa155 on https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/475.

The golden guest account password is no longer admin. It is a random value in ~/.c11-sandbox/guest-password on Atlas, mode 600. Auto-login's /etc/kcpassword matches it. Password SSH stays off. The grant notes at /tmp/c11-244-grant.md read the password from that file and do not contain it.

Checked by rebooting the golden guest: console user was admin, Finder was frontmost, sudo -n still worked, and dscl auth against the new password succeeded. The golden image was then stopped. scanner-base and scanner-golden were left stopped. The Ghostty probe from the earlier commit was not repeated.

No password was committed.

Repair push 7d453fb0c966f75d5d0e78105ac740ad86bd54ac on https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/475.

Opus review of 7d64986d failed because every clone passed --random-serial, so Setup Assistant's FileVault sheet held key focus. The 2fc5aace app-source seam is unchanged.

A single clone now keeps the golden serial and always passes --random-mac. --allow-second is the only path that passes --random-serial, and that second guest may show Setup Assistant. There is no installed profile.

Proven from the laptop with C11_SANDBOX_HOST unset: sandbox-up repair1 of a released .app returned clone_secs=0 and boot_secs=29, and tart run stayed up after that SSH session closed. docs/images/c11-244-no-setup.png shows Aqua with no Setup Assistant. One cliclick closed the restored System Settings window. docs/images/c11-244-click.png shows the four terminals in front. sandbox-down repair1 deleted the clone. The golden image and both scanner VMs stayed stopped.

Also in this commit: a mkdir lock around the cap check and clone; EXIT, INT, and HUP cleanup removes the staged app; sandbox-down is the recovery when a session drops; tests_v2 continues after a failing file and prints summary passed=N failed=M; the doc says the suite must match the app build; CLAUDE.md names C11_SOCKET, C11_SOCKET_PATH, and C11_CLI; the unused mobileconfig is removed.

The guest password was already rotated in a6815d091. It was not rotated again. It lives at ~/.c11-sandbox/guest-password on Atlas, mode 600. It is not in the repo.

CI was green before this comment. Do not merge. Do not mark the ticket done. After merge, the maintainer runs scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh c11-computer-use. The installed skill was not synced from this worktree.

Repair push db0414fdcc0fb29462bd88b0b5bbbe1f49053d7a on https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/475.

Delta re-review of 7d453fb0 passed. This commit is the one fix it asked for before merge.

Reusing a live run id used to hit the existing-VM check after the failure trap, with failed=1. Cleanup then stopped that clone, killed the pid in its tart.pid, and removed its staged app. sandbox-up now refuses that id before it stages a new app. The same check inside the clone lock sets failed=0 before it exits, so cleanup only releases the lock and the live clone stays up.

An empty lock pid means the owner is still writing it. Waiters retry instead of taking the lock. A dead pid is still replaced.

bash -n passed. shellcheck reports only the pre-existing SC1091 info on the source line; warning level is clean. A local zsh check confirmed an empty pid is not stolen, a dead pid is replaced, and the duplicate-id exit leaves the staged app and the tart pid in place.

CI was green before this comment. Do not merge. Do not mark the ticket done. After merge, the maintainer runs scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh c11-computer-use. The installed skill was not synced from this worktree.

PR #475 squash-merged to main as 1d5f5fa89977144f5daedf91f674d8fb9644d9be. Design approved by Atin (headless Tart VMs, hosted on Atlas, host configurable via C11_SANDBOX_HOST). Tart 2.32.1, Fair Source 0.9 (Cirrus Labs). Proven: Ghostty renders in guest (docs/images/c11-244-guest-terminal.png; debug-terminals runtime=1); default laptop->atlas path: sandbox-up boot 29s, no Setup Assistant on single clone (golden serial kept; --random-serial only for a second concurrent clone), cliclick closed a window (docs/images/c11-244-click.png), sandbox-down deleted clone; tests_v2 file passed inside guest. Reviews: Opus FAIL at 7d64986d (Setup Assistant on every clone) -> repaired; Sonnet delta PASS at 7d453fb0; final one-commit fix (duplicate run-id no longer deletes a live clone; empty-pid lock wait) attested by orchestrator at db0414fd. CI green. Guest password rotated to ~/.c11-sandbox/guest-password on Atlas. Skill sync deferred: Release Captain triggers after 0.67.0 install. Follow-up seam: atlas-build app source once Xcode is on Atlas.
